question: After the unconditional Shatter state, repeated Shatter and Resonant Lance reader are removed, does exact current-main expose one canonical downstream Shatter consumer that is structurally distinct from every closed Dusk family?
scientificBasis: A realised Dusk Shatter writes one enemy-local staggered boolean. Exact enemy-phase order first resolves lethal Smolder, then either consumes that boolean by emitting STAGGERED and skipping the already-authored current move, or executes the move. Exact source already defines a native binary boundary: preview_enemy_dmg returns null for a non-damaging intent and a damage forecast otherwise, and the current pilot removes staggered enemies from incoming-damage forecasts. This permits one source-defined damaging-authored-action suppression relation without inventing a payoff, threshold, card, intent label or optimiser.

frontierScope.included: The complete lifecycle of the existing enemy-local staggered boolean from realised Shatter through player-phase readers, lethal pre-emption and enemy-phase consumption, partitioned by the exact authored current move's native damage/non-damage boundary.
excluded: Facet production, threshold, same-target reseam or cross-target topology
generic Shatter count, vulnerable, Ember, draw, Energy or global power
Resonant Lance damage echo or another player-phase stagger reader
poison transfer, enemy death, relic aftermath or fight-quality reward
pooling block, heal, buff and debuff moves into one non-damage scalar
card, enemy, act, formation, intent-label or damage-magnitude subset
payoff, carrier, acquisition, policy score, telemetry, ML, RL or optimiser
trace, cache, outcome or policy support
frontierScope.claimBoundary: This source-only audit may freeze at most one exact existing relation for a separate zero-new-row observability and upper-capacity preregistration. It cannot establish realised support, policy selectivity, causal benefit, complementarity, package admission, a research knob or product authority.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: No realised Shatter writes staggered, combat ends first, ordinary damage kills the enemy, or enemy-phase Smolder kills it before the stagger branch; no STAGGERED action skip occurs.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: There is no enemy-action suppression mediator. Treating Shatter count or its unconditional outputs as sufficient would reopen the rejected generic family.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: A further realised Shatter writes true over an already-true boolean before enemy-phase consumption and therefore cannot suppress a second action.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: The boolean has no additional action-suppression state. Selecting repeat count or a harder pane would reopen the closed same-enemy reseam family.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: Before enemy phase, Resonant Lance may read staggered as one of two conditions for its damage multiplier.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: This is the exact rejected Resonant Lance shatterEcho package, not enemy-action suppression.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: After Smolder, STAGGERED skips a current move with no authored dmg field.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: The 47 moves divide into block, heal, buff and debuff actions with four distinct effect signatures. Pooling them would invent one scalar outcome; this audit neither selects nor closes any separately justified member.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: After Smolder, STAGGERED consumes a living enemy's current authored move whose definition contains dmg, appends the move key to history and emits no ENEMY_ACT for that action.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: This is an existing producer-consumer handshake between a Dusk-only realised Shatter and the downstream enemy action gate. It is not a new payoff after every Shatter, player-phase echo damage, player action economy or post-fight no-loss reward.

actionSuppressionPartition.definition: After either a skipped or executed action, Ritual gain and vulnerable/weak ticks still run.
actionSuppressionPartition.reason: These transitions are explicitly not suppressed by stagger and therefore are fixed downstream context, not part of the selected action gate.

selectedRelation.name: Shatter interruption of a damaging authored intent
selectedRelation.exactPredicate: In enemy phase after Smolder resolution, a living enemy enters the existing staggered branch and its current move definition has a dmg field; STAGGERED is emitted and ENEMY_ACT for that move is absent.
selectedRelation.nativeBoundary: preview_enemy_dmg is non-null for the current move
selectedRelation.actionScope: The whole authored damaging action is suppressed, including any attached block, heal, status, ramp, repeat or add-card effect. Those signatures are fixed natural heterogeneity, not separately varied factors.

mechanisticInteractions.poisonPreemption: Enemy-phase Smolder resolves first. A lethal tick removes the enemy and its stagger state, so only an actual STAGGERED event can establish consumption.
mechanisticInteractions.compoundMoves: Fifty-five damaging moves include another authored effect or repetition. A later estimand must treat the whole action gate as the factor and report direct-damage forecast plus signature strata without claiming pure damage mediation.
mechanisticInteractions.multipleEnemies: All 54 formations contain at least one damaging-capable enemy, but target choice can matter only in multi-enemy state. A later capacity screen must measure rather than assume policy selectivity.
mechanisticInteractions.playerDefence: Player Ward, Weak, Vulnerable, Warding Charm and difficulty modifiers alter forecast damage but not the authored damage/non-damage boundary.
mechanisticInteractions.anchors: Scoreline and Afterimage remain separate fixed activation anchors. Neither payoff is varied or estimated here.

capacityEvidenceBoundary.precondition: A separate protocol must freeze the one eligible identity-safe current-main trace, exact INTENT-to-STAGGERED parser, poison/death exclusion, move-definition join, robust active/inactive/viable policy gates, separate Scoreline and Afterimage anchors, reliability, wall-time and all decision rules before opening any trace or cache.
capacityEvidenceBoundary.observabilityRule: If the eligible trace lacks enemy idx, move identity, turn/fight identity or actual STAGGERED consumption, stop at an observability boundary without adding or repairing telemetry.
capacityEvidenceBoundary.causalBoundary: No research factor is authorised by this audit. Only a successful capacity result may justify a separately preregistered, identity-proven consumer-local factor that leaves Shatter production, Resonant Lance, non-damaging skips, RNG and all unrelated state unchanged.

decisionRules.success: The six-cell lifecycle partition is source-complete with exactly one selected existing relation; all source, content, evidence and ledger identities pass without reading support, trace or cache, and execution finishes within 30 seconds.
decisionRules.successAuthority: Apply decision boundary 1 and freeze only enemy-phase-damaging-intent-skip for one separately preregistered zero-new-row observability and capacity screen. Do not open a trace before its parser and gates are frozen, implement a factor, add telemetry, simulate, add a ledger row, use a protected seed or claim a package.
decisionRules.futility: No unique, canonical and unclosed downstream Shatter consumer remains.
decisionRules.futilityAuthority: Apply decision boundary 2 and close this Shatter action-suppression frontier. Continue inside issue #421 from another source-complete structural mechanism; do not reopen generic Shatter, Resonant Lance, repeat Shatter or pool heterogeneous non-damage actions.
decisionRules.inconclusive: Any partition, source, content, evidence or ledger identity fails, more than one relation is selected, or execution exceeds 30 seconds.
decisionRules.inconclusiveAuthority: Apply decision boundary 3 and record the audit inconclusive at cap without reading support, selecting a factor, adding telemetry, simulating, adding a row, using a method or protected seed.
